description:
Both `docs/historian/token_usage.py query` and `docs/historian/historian.py` build their commit list with `git log --no-merges`, so every trailer stamped on a MERGE commit is excluded from the reported token totals.

Measured on origin/develop at 2e085b2 (2026-08-06):

  trailered commits, all:        247   total 5,876,958,905
  trailered commits, non-merge:  172   total 3,363,701,768   <- what query reports
  trailered commits, merge only:  75   total 2,513,257,137   <- silently dropped

That is 42.8% of the recorded token spend.

Why this looks unintended rather than deliberate: CLAUDE.md's historian section says lines come from 'git log --numstat --no-merges' and describes the merge exclusion for LINES only. Excluding merges is correct for lines (a merge re-reports its side branch's lines). It is wrong for tokens, because each API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit trailer is a DISJOINT delta -- prepare-commit-msg stamps the delta since the previous commit and post-commit advances the baseline, so a merge commit's trailer is real work not counted anywhere else. In this workspace merge commits are where the expensive part lives: reading the diff, running per-crate release tests, Android --all-targets, provenance and sign-off checks.

Largest dropped trailers:
  205,934,989  26080c16  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  186,299,135  423a5db3  Merge branch 'claude/outram-blender-mggk7u' into develop
  175,539,906  0d949263  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  130,215,239  53b5bef9  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop

Sites: token_usage.py cmd_query line ~329; historian.py line ~85.

Suggested fix: drop --no-merges from the TOKEN commit list in both tools while keeping it for the numstat/lines path, and report merge-commit tokens as a separate line so the split stays visible. Needs the maintainer's confirmation that counting merge commits is the intended semantics before any code change -- this bead is the finding, not an authorisation to edit.

(Re-filed 2026-08-12. Originally created 2026-08-07 as op-25z on a container-local beads store ref that was still format_version 1 and never reached the shared store; that ref is preserved at refs/beads/premigration-local-op25z-20260812. Content unchanged from the original.)
title: token accounting: query + historian drop merge-commit trailers (43% of recorded tokens invisible)

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme / #77).

Extends the refinery into an integrated refinery/petrochemical/polymer complex.
**Do not implement the whole complex in this pass.**

## Target chain

```
CRUDE -> DESALTER -> CDU -+-> NAPHTHA -> HDT -+-> CATALYTIC REFORMING -> reformate -> BTX
                          |                    +-> STEAM CRACKER -> ethylene/propylene/C4/pygas
                          +-> MIDDLE DISTILLATES                          |
                          +-> ATM RESIDUE -> VDU -> VGO / VR              v
                                                                   MONOMERS -> POLYMERS
```

Track crude-derived carbon conservatively through crude -> refinery fractions
-> olefins/aromatics -> monomers -> polymers, while accounting for nuclear
process heat, hydrogen, electricity, steam, CO2, coke, sulfur, nitrogen,
wastewater, flare and stack emissions.

## Architecture (unchanged, binding)

```
outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs   <- steady process physics
        ^
outram-foam-appbuilder-lib    <- adapts to spatial/transient FVM
        v
Outram-FOAM FVM
```

**DWSIM must not depend on Outram-FOAM. Do not duplicate chemical kinetics
inside Outram-FOAM.**

## Audit performed while filing (2026-09-05)

### Already present and reusable

- **LHHW / heterogeneous catalytic kinetics** — `langmuir_hinshelwood_rate`,
  `with_langmuir_hinshelwood`, `adsorption_constant`, `denominator_value`,
  Arrhenius forward/reverse constants, `equilibrium_constant`,
  `with_reaction_heat`, `ReactionKind`, `ReactionBasis`. **The reusable
  framework this brief asks for exists.** Reforming and hydroprocessing need
  reaction *networks*, not new kinetics infrastructure, and must not get
  hard-coded `PlatformerRateEquation`-style solvers.
- **Reactors** — `Pfr`, `Cstr`, `ConversionReactor`, `EquilibriumReactor`,
  `GibbsReactor`.
- **Unit operations** — compressor, expander, cooler, heater, heat_exchanger,
  mixer, splitter, separator, pump, pipe, valve, flowsheet, flowsheet_solver,
  dynamics.
- **Thermo (35 files)** — cubic EOS incl. PR-1978 / PRSV2 / PR-Lee-Kesler /
  LKP / Chao-Seader-Grayson, activity models incl. UNIFAC / UNIFAC-Dortmund /
  **UNIFAC-LLE**, electrolyte, electrolyte SVLE, sour water, seawater,
  stability, transport, Gibbs, multiphase Gibbs; flashes VLE / VLLE / **LLE** /
  SLE / SVLLE / inside-out / 3-phase inside-out / immiscible / energy.
  **UNIFAC-LLE plus an LLE flash is the basis for BTX extraction** — audit
  before writing extraction models.

### Missing entirely

- **Polymer representation.** No moments, no MWD, no chain-length bins. The
  only textual hit is `pem_fuel_cell.rs` (polymer *electrolyte membrane*), a
  false positive. **All polymer work is new.**
- No dedicated extraction unit operation, no refrigeration/cryogenic package.
- No steam-cracking (free-radical thermal) kinetics.

### The blocking defect

`ColumnType` has four variants but **only `distillation` has a constructor**.
`AbsorptionColumn`, `ReboiledAbsorber` and `RefluxedAbsorber` are unreachable,
blocking AGR, cracked-gas absorbers, side strippers, the reformate stabilizer
and a structurally correct CDU. Filed separately as a P0 blocker — it is the
cheapest item in either programme relative to what it unblocks.

## Fidelity labels (binding)

Crude estimate / Engineering model / Predictive model. **Do not upgrade a label
merely because the solver converges.**

## Conservation (binding)

Representation changes crude assay -> CDU pseudocomponents -> reaction lumps ->
small molecules -> **polymer moments** must preserve mass, C, H, O, N, S, **Cl
where PVC chemistry is present**, and metals/catalyst inventories.

**Polymerization must not lose mass because thousands of chain lengths are
represented through moments.**

## Not to do

Implement the whole complex; port DWSIM UI or CAPE-OPEN without concrete need;
build monolithic `EthylenePlant` / `PolyethylenePlant` solvers; track thousands
of molecules through every CDU tray; track every polymer molecule explicitly;
duplicate chemistry in Outram-FOAM; sacrifice conservation during lumping;
treat black-oil results as predictive; hide recycle/conservation failures;
**merge or push to `main`**.
title: Integrated petrochemical and polymer platform

description:
DISCOVERED 2026-08-05 while investigating an apparent total loss of the tracker (which turned out to be operator error -- bd was being run from inside the vendored OpenFOAM clone, which is its own git repo, so it hashed a different repo identity and opened an empty store; fixed by returning to the workspace root, all 615 issues intact).

THE REAL FINDING, which is not operator error: this container's beads data is NOT durable.

CLAUDE.md states the canonical store lives in git refs -- refs/heads/beads/store holding state/deps/tombstones jsonl plus meta.json, with backups under refs/beads/backup/* -- and that a background 'bd daemon' auto-syncs that ref to the remote.

Measured here:
  git for-each-ref 'refs/heads/beads/*' 'refs/beads/*'   -> NOTHING
  git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/beads/*' 'refs/beads/*' -> NOTHING

So neither the local repo nor the remote carries any beads ref. The only copy of all 615 issues is the local beads-rs store under /root/.local/share/beads-rs/ (WAL 43a04eb0a133bcfd.wal plus the JSONL export). This container is ephemeral and is reclaimed after inactivity, so if it goes, the tracker goes with it -- including every bead filed this session.

MITIGATION TAKEN: a 615-issue JSONL export and the WAL were copied to the session scratchpad. That is also ephemeral, so it is insurance for the next few hours only, not a fix.

WHAT THE MAINTAINER NEEDS TO DECIDE:
- whether a bd daemon should be running in this container at all, and if so how it authenticates to push refs/heads/beads/store;
- or whether beads should simply be treated as local-only in remote containers, with an explicit export committed before a session ends;
- note bd 0.1.26 here has NO import subcommand, so a JSONL export cannot be re-ingested by bd -- recovery from the export would be manual or need a newer bd.

Also worth guarding: bd silently opens a NEW EMPTY STORE when run from a different git repo rather than erroring. Running it one directory too deep -- inside any vendored upstream clone -- looks exactly like total data loss. Worth a kopitiam-style issue upstream to beads-rs.

---
RE-FILED 2026-08-12 with its original id. This bead was created in an earlier session but never published, because beads-rs `bd` could not push the store ref (kopitiam#19). It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: open.
title: beads store in this container is NOT backed by git refs

description:
Pipeline run for MSRE (ORNL, 8 MWth). Existing: op-6w0 (MSRE digital twin epic), docs/reactor-scoping/msre.md.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST TO THIS WORKSPACE: outram-park-fork-moltres exists precisely for circulating-fuel physics — precursor drift, salt thermal, coupled solver — and it is the ONE crate whose execution seams already reach Python in full (CoupledMsrSolver, CirculatingFuelSolver, PrecursorDrift, RingMesh). It is the least blocked reactor in the set and the natural first pipeline run.
TARGETS: zero-power criticality, the reactivity loss from precursor drift as a function of fuel-pump circulation time (the MSRE-defining measurement and the reason the code exists), the salt temperature/density coefficient, and the pump-coastdown/loss-of-flow transient.
ENDF NEEDED: U-235 (have), Li-7, Be-9, F-19, Zr, O-16, plus Th-232/U-233 for the later 233U core (all missing). The salt is the gap.
HARDEST STAGE: MGXS. moltres IS a multigroup diffusion code, so it cannot run at all without op-84bc, and it needs the library re-collapsed as salt temperature and density move — the parametrised form, not a fixed set.
NOTE: the MSRE 233U core is a separately documented benchmark from the 235U core. Pick one and say which.

Parent: op-wpi0

description:
BLOCKS EVERY REACTOR CHILD. Decide before any of them starts.

raffles/src/surrogate.rs is 54 lines with NO pub items — a stub. sensitivity.rs is real (Sobol sample layout, Pearson and Spearman correlation, input-output correlations) but that is sampling and sensitivity, not a surrogate: there is no GP, no polynomial chaos, no POD, no response surface of any kind.

So the requested chain — ENDF -> MC -> MGXS+feedback -> deterministic -> ROM -> digital twin — has a hole at stage 5.

TWO OPTIONS, and it is a maintainer call because it changes every reactor child:

  (a) IMPLEMENT. The sampling half already exists, so the work is the model: a Gaussian process or polynomial-chaos surrogate over the state grid the MGXS work (op-84bc) will already be producing. Those two compose naturally — the same state grid of temperature/density/burnup feeds both.

  (b) DROP IT for now. Go deterministic -> digital twin directly. The twin runs the deterministic model at real-time rates or it does not; a surrogate is an optimisation, not a requirement, and every reactor child gets simpler.

WHAT DECIDES IT is whether the deterministic stage is fast enough to drive a twin at interactive rates for the reactor in question. That is measurable and should be measured on one reactor before committing: run the genfoam/bedok/moltres solve for a representative transient, time it, and compare against the twin's tick budget. If it clears, (b). If it does not, (a) and the surrogate is load-bearing rather than decorative.

Parent: op-wpi0

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
SUPERSEDED by op-38my / gh:#44, which covers the same decision across BOTH crates rather than only as a pipeline blocker.

The reason for the split: this bead framed stage 5 purely as 'does the validation pipeline need a ROM'. That undersells it. raffles is a RAVEN port and ROM is RAVEN's own first-class concept, so its absence is a gap in the port itself, independent of any pipeline. And tampines needs a tabulation/surrogate layer for real-time twin operation whatever the pipeline decides — the property and closure evaluations are the inner loop of every transient.

Keep this bead as op-wpi0's gate: the pipeline still cannot start its reactor children until the stage-5 question is answered. But the answer, and the work either way, live in op-38my.

title: Pipeline stage 5 decision: implement a surrogate in raffles, or drop ROM from the chain
